reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation / Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics
clinicalPearls: A distinctive face with a broad prominent forehead, deep-set widely spaced eyes, a saddle nose with a rounded tip, and uplifted fleshy earlobes (the classic 'orecchiette' or medially raised lobes) is highly recognisable
Hirschsprung disease or severe chronic constipation is a major and characteristic association
Caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants or deletions of ZEB2, following autosomal dominant inheritance and almost always de novo
Severe intellectual disability with absent or very limited speech but a notably happy, sociable demeanour is typical
Microcephaly, epilepsy and agenesis or hypoplasia of the corpus callosum are frequent
Congenital heart disease and genitourinary anomalies including hypospadias are common
The combination of the facial gestalt with Hirschsprung disease should prompt ZEB2 testing
reference.pathophysiology: Mowat-Wilson syndrome is caused by haploinsufficiency of ZEB2, a transcription factor (also called SIP1) that represses target genes and is essential for the development and migration of neural crest cells and for central nervous system patterning. Loss-of-function point variants and whole-gene deletions reduce ZEB2 activity, disrupting neural crest derivatives, which explains the enteric nervous system defect underlying Hirschsprung disease as well as the craniofacial, cardiac and genitourinary malformations, together with the neurodevelopmental impairment from disturbed brain development.
additionalInvestigations: Sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis of ZEB2, or chromosomal microarray to detect deletions
Rectal suction biopsy and contrast studies to confirm Hirschsprung disease when suspected
Brain MRI to assess the corpus callosum and other structural anomalies
Renal tract ultrasound and genitourinary assessment
redFlags: Bilious vomiting, abdominal distension or enterocolitis suggesting Hirschsprung-related obstruction
Undiagnosed congenital heart disease causing cardiorespiratory compromise
Signs of Hirschsprung-associated enterocolitis, a potentially life-threatening complication
reference.prognosis: Individuals typically have severe intellectual disability with lifelong dependency but a characteristically cheerful temperament; survival into adulthood is common with appropriate management of bowel, cardiac and neurological complications. Enterocolitis and cardiac disease are the main threats to life.
pitfalls: Diagnosing isolated Hirschsprung disease without recognising an associated syndrome
Missing corpus callosum agenesis that supports the diagnosis
Overlooking genitourinary anomalies such as hypospadias
Failing to consider ZEB2 testing when the facial gestalt is present without overt bowel disease
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: Manage Hirschsprung disease surgically by resecting the aganglionic segment, and treat severe chronic constipation with an intensive bowel regimen
Maintain vigilance for enterocolitis, a leading and potentially fatal complication requiring prompt treatment
Control epilepsy with anticonvulsants and monitor with electroencephalography
Assess and surgically repair congenital heart disease and genitourinary anomalies such as hypospadias
Provide neurodevelopmental and communication support with early intervention, special education, alternative communication and physiotherapy
Offer genetic counselling, noting the autosomal dominant and almost always de novo nature with a small recurrence risk from germline mosaicism
Coordinate multidisciplinary care across paediatric surgery, cardiology, neurology and clinical genetics
